name: Latvia
tagline: Cheap, close to Denmark, and the Nordic route into medicine
summary: Latvia is a three-hour flight from Denmark, uses the euro, and charges a fraction of what the UK or the Netherlands charge. There is no central admissions system for international students: you apply directly to each university, and the one step you cannot skip is getting your IB Diploma recognised by the Academic Information Centre. The real draw is Riga Stradins University, whose English-taught medicine and dentistry programmes take large numbers of Scandinavian students who did not get a place at home.
whyConsider: Tuition is low by European standards - some bachelor programmes are under EUR 1,600 a year
English-taught medicine and dentistry at RSU, with no Danish quota standing in the way
Living costs in Riga are roughly EUR 450-700 a month
As an EU citizen you just register; no visa, no health surcharge
Stockholm School of Economics in Riga is a genuinely selective, Swedish-run business school with a heavily subsidised EU fee
watchOuts: There is no central portal - you apply to each university separately and each has its own deadlines and fees
You must pay for and obtain an AIC recognition statement for your IB Diploma before a university can admit you (EUR 54.60)
Medicine at RSU is not cheap: EUR 13,500 a year plus a one-off EUR 1,800 registration administration fee
Outside medicine, business and a few IT programmes, English-taught bachelor choice is thinner than in Lithuania
Latvian is the language of daily life; you will be fine at university but not automatically in a part-time job

ibRecognition.subjectLevelRule: Set by each university and each programme rather than nationally. RSU's admissions system applies programme-specific subject requirements; the exact IB subject and grade rules are not published; ask the programme.
ibRecognition.gradeConversion: The Academic Information Centre (AIC) compares your foreign qualification with the Latvian education system and issues a recognition statement, which the university then uses as the basis for its admission decision. No IB-to-Latvian grade conversion table is published.
notes: Academic recognition is compulsory, not optional: the University of Latvia states that recognition 'is required if the student holds a foreign qualification (diploma) and wishes to continue their studies in Latvia', and that an application can be rejected if the recognition is not positive.
Recognition costs EUR 54.60 (the fee is now set by Cabinet Regulation No. 281 of 13 May 2025, same amount as before). AIC says its statement is prepared within a month - start it early.
AIC is Latvia's ENIC/NARIC centre and was set up by the Ministry of Education and Science in 1994.
Minimum IB points are set per programme, not nationally - check each programme page.

portal.name: Study in Latvia (national information portal; applications go direct to each university)

deadlines.label: Turiba University - autumn intake
deadlines.year: Published without a year on 2026-09-22; expect the same window for the autumn 2027 intake but re-check
deadlines.notes: Published as "From February 1 to August 1", with no year given, so the year here is inferred from the intake this profile covers. Studies begin at the end of September. Turiba also runs a winter intake, "From August 2 to December 1" for a February start; that is a different intake, which is why it has no card of its own: a May 2027 IB candidate cannot start in February 2027 and would be looking at February 2028. All Turiba programmes are available in both intakes.

deadlines.label: Riga Stradins University - International Business & Start-up Entrepreneurship, September 2027 intake, EU/EEA applicants
deadlines.notes: RSU's table prints the opening as "1 Sep 2025", which is the previous intake's date: the master's row for the same intake reads "1 Sep 2026 – 1 Jul 2027", and the February tab opens this programme on 1 Sep 2026. So the window opened on 1 September 2026 and is open now. The date that matters is the close, 1 July 2027, which is not in doubt.

deadlines.label: Riga Stradins University - September 2027 intake, EU/EEA applicants (Medicine and Dentistry)
deadlines.notes: Published as "1 Mar – 1 Jul 2027". Worth knowing before you plan around the July closing date: RSU allows IB graduates, alongside German Abitur holders and applicants from Italy, Portugal and the Netherlands, to send their school graduation documents after the deadline provided every other application document is in by it. That concession is published on this page with the previous cycle's year on it ("graduating during the summer of 2026 … submitted by 1 July 2026") and RSU had not restated it for 2027 by 23 September 2026, so confirm it with RSU admissions before you rely on it.

deadlines.label: Riga Stradins University - September 2027 intake, non-EU/EEA applicants
deadlines.notes: Non-EU applicants close earlier than EU applicants to leave time for the residence permit.

deadlines.label: Riga Stradins University - September 2027 intake, applicants from 'Additional Assessment' countries
deadlines.notes: Published inside the non-EU/EEA window as "1 March 2027 to 1 May 2027 (1 April 2027 for citizens of 'Additional Assessment' countries)". Non-EU applicants close earlier than EU applicants to leave time for the residence permit.

deadlines.label: Stockholm School of Economics in Riga - BSc application deadline
deadlines.notes: Published as "April 6, 2027". Top 150 candidates are admitted.

deadlines.label: Stockholm School of Economics in Riga - admissions test
deadlines.notes: Published as "April 17, 2027, starting at 10:00" Eastern European Time — eleven days after the application closes, so there is no time to prepare for it once you have applied. Prepare before 6 April, not after.

deadlines.label: Stockholm School of Economics in Riga - online interviews for top performers
deadlines.notes: Published as "from May 11 till May 28, 2027". Only candidates who do well in the 17 April test are invited, and the window falls squarely across the May 2027 IB examination session — so if SSE Riga is on your list, expect to be interviewed during your exams and plan for it now rather than in May.

deadlines.label: Stockholm School of Economics in Riga - results, EU applicants
deadlines.notes: Published as "June 8, 2027" for applicants from EU countries; applicants from non-EU countries hear four days earlier, on 4 June 2027, which is context rather than your date.

deadlines.label: Stockholm School of Economics in Riga - registration deadline, EU applicants
deadlines.notes: Published as "July 25, 2027" for applicants from EU countries. This is the day an offer stops being yours: you have from 8 June to register, and a place you have not registered by this date is gone. Non-EU applicants must register by 20 June 2027, over a month earlier, to leave time for a residence permit — not your deadline, but it explains why the EU date is the later one. Studies begin 23 August 2027.

deadlines.label: Riga Stradins University - February 2027 intake, EU/EEA applicants (Medicine and Dentistry)
deadlines.notes: RSU’s "when to apply" page has a February 2027 tab giving "4 Sep – 1 Dec 2026" for EU/EEA and visa-free applicants, with 1 Oct 2026 for Additional Assessment countries and 1 Nov 2026 for other non-EU applicants. Read the intake before you read the window: this one starts in February 2027, months before a May 2027 IB session finishes, so it is not a route for you. It is shown because RSU runs two intakes a year and this is the trap - a window that appears to be open now and is not yours. If you want a February start, it is February 2028 you are looking at.

readerAccess.reason: This intake starts in February 2027, before a May 2027 IB Diploma is awarded, so a May 2027 candidate cannot use it.

steps: Pick the programme first. There is no national application system for international students, so your deadlines are whatever the university says they are.
Apply to the Academic Information Centre for recognition of your IB Diploma. It costs EUR 54.60 and the university cannot admit you without a positive statement.
Submit the university's own online application with your transcript, passport and proof of English, and pay the application fee (EUR 100 at RSU, EUR 250 at Turiba).
Sit whatever the programme requires: RSU runs programme-specific assessments, SSE Riga runs a four-hour online test in April followed by interviews in May.

Accept the offer and sign the study agreement. RSU expects payment within two weeks of receiving the offer, and charges medicine and dentistry students a one-off EUR 1,800 registration administration fee.
As an EU citizen, travel to Latvia freely, then complete the registration formalities and collect a Registration Card if you are staying more than three months.
application.selectionNotes: Selection is per programme. Medicine and dentistry at RSU are competitive and close earlier for non-EU applicants. SSE Riga is the most selective route in the country: it requires minimum grades of 6 on a scale of 10 in Mathematics and English, runs its own admissions test covering mathematical reasoning, logical thinking and English, interviews the top performers, and takes 150 students. Latvia does operate state-funded ('budget') study places, but whether an EU citizen from Denmark can compete for them is not confirmed here; ask the university.

language.englishTaughtBachelors: Moderate. Concentrated in medicine and health at RSU, business at SSE Riga, Turiba and BA School of Business and Finance, and engineering/IT at RTU. Outside those areas the choice thins out quickly. No exact national count is published.
language.englishProof: Each university sets its own standard. Turiba requires its own English test unless you hold a certificate, and accepts IELTS 5.5, TOEFL iBT 72, TOEFL PBT 513, TOEIC 605, Cambridge FCE/CAE/CPE 160, PTE Academic 51, Linguaskill 160, Duolingo 100 or LanguageCert ESOL B2. SSE Riga requires B2, certified by an international testing authority for applicants educated outside the EU. Whether IB English A or B is accepted in place of a test is not confirmed here - ask the programme directly.
notes: Programmes advertised as English-taught are taught fully in English; Latvian is not required for the degree.
Russian is still widely spoken in Riga alongside Latvian, which surprises some students.

tuitionEuEea.value: Varies entirely by university. Study in Latvia states tuition 'range from less than EUR 1 600 per year for certain bachelor's degree programmes (3-4 years of studies)' upwards. SSE Riga charges EU/EEA/EFTA students EUR 5,200 a year after an automatic EUR 2,400 Baltic-EU scholarship is deducted from the EUR 7,600 list price. RSU does not distinguish EU from non-EU rates.
tuitionEuEea.year: Study in Latvia figure undated on its page; SSE Riga figure current as published on 2026-09-22

tuitionNonEu.value: RSU 2026/2027: Medicine EUR 13,500 a year (6-year programme), Dentistry EUR 15,500 a year (5-year programme), International Business & Start-up Entrepreneurship EUR 3,300 a year - the same rates apply to EU and non-EU students. SSE Riga: EUR 7,600 a year for non-EU/EEA/EFTA students, EUR 22,800 over the three-year programme.

costs.applicationFee: RSU EUR 100 (EUR 30 for Latvian citizens), plus a one-off registration administration fee of EUR 1,800 for Medicine and Dentistry. Turiba EUR 250, non-refundable.

livingCostMonthly.value: EUR 450-700 a month, covering food, housing, utilities, transport and everyday costs, depending on accommodation and lifestyle
livingCostMonthly.year: Undated on the source page (as of September 2026)

notes: Add EUR 54.60 for the compulsory AIC recognition of your IB Diploma.
RSU's fees are payable by semester, due within two weeks of receiving the offer of a study place.
SSE Riga fees are fixed for all three years of the programme.

funding: SSE Riga runs the most substantial scholarship scheme found: an automatic EUR 2,400 Baltic-EU scholarship for EU/EEA/EFTA students, up to 20 competitive admissions scholarships giving partial or full tuition waivers for one to three years, merit awards of EUR 300-2,000, and an SEB bank loan programme guaranteed by the school. In 2025, 47 bachelor students shared EUR 218,080 in scholarships.
Latvian state-guaranteed student loans are mentioned by SSE Riga as available; eligibility for an EU/EEA citizen who is not resident in Latvia is not confirmed here; ask SSE Riga.

funding.note: The programme must be SU-approved, and outside the Nordics SU is capped at four years (48 klip).

funding: Individual universities run their own merit scholarships; check each programme page.
workRights: A full-time bachelor's student at a Latvian university may work up to 20 hours a week during term and up to 40 hours a week during holidays. Master's and doctoral students have no restriction. The Study in Latvia FAQ does not distinguish EU from non-EU students on this point, but non-EU students additionally need a work permit arranged with the employer.
residency: As an EU/EEA citizen you can travel to Latvia freely and stay three months with no immigration procedure at all. For a longer stay you complete registration formalities with the Office of Citizenship and Migration Affairs and receive a Registration Card. Non-EU students must obtain a residence permit before arriving in Latvia, arranged through the university's international office. After finishing a bachelor's degree, non-EU graduates get four months to find further study or work.
housing: Universities run dormitories and most international offices help arrange a room; RSU's 'Your Start in Riga' pages cover this. Private rental in Riga is cheap by Nordic standards and there is no housing shortage of the kind you see in Copenhagen or Amsterdam. Arrange it once you have accepted an offer.
healthcare: As an EU citizen bring your European Health Insurance Card (EHIC, the blue card) from the country where you are insured for necessary care. Latvia's public system covers emergencies; most international students also take out private insurance. Non-EU students must arrange insurance as part of the residence permit application.

institutions.name: University of Latvia
institutions.englishBachelors: A small number, mostly in business, IT and social sciences; no exact count is published
institutions.note: Clear on its own pages about the AIC recognition requirement, with a small number of English-taught bachelor's in business, IT and social sciences.

institutions.name: Riga Technical University
institutions.englishBachelors: Eleven English-taught bachelor's listed on its application portal (2026-09-24): a BBA at Riga Business School and BSc degrees in civil, mechanical, environmental, materials and medical engineering, computer systems, electronics, telecommunications, finance information systems and entrepreneurship
institutions.note: The main engineering university in Latvia and the home of Riga Business School. Since 1 March 2024 the former Liepaja University is part of it as RTU Liepaja. rtu.lv blocks automated reading, so fees and deadlines were not checked - look on apply.rtu.lv.

institutions.name: Riga Stradins University
institutions.englishBachelors: Medicine, Dentistry and a set of health and social science programmes in English, plus International Business & Start-up Entrepreneurship
institutions.note: The reason most Scandinavians look at Latvia: a large English-taught medical intake with two intakes a year, Medicine at EUR 13,500 and Dentistry at EUR 15,500 for 2026/2027.

institutions.name: Stockholm School of Economics in Riga
institutions.englishBachelors: One: a three-year BSc, taught entirely in English
institutions.note: Swedish-run, admits 150 students a year after its own April test and May interviews, and charges EU students EUR 5,200 a year after an automatic scholarship.

institutions.name: Turiba University
institutions.englishBachelors: Several business, tourism, communication and law programmes in English
institutions.note: A business university teaching business, tourism, communication and law in English; applies a rolling 1 February to 1 August window for the autumn intake and charges a EUR 250 application fee.

institutions.name: BA School of Business and Finance
institutions.englishBachelors: Three in English: Business Process Management, Finance Management Information Systems and International Finance
institutions.note: Small, finance-focused and founded by the Bank of Latvia; a practical alternative if SSE Riga is out of reach. On 1 September 2026 it changed its name to the UL FinTech Business School; it was already part of the University of Latvia, so this is a rename rather than a merger, and its site is now ftbs.lu.lv. Expect to meet the new name on application forms and the old one in rankings and prospectuses for some years yet.

institutions.name: Latvia University of Life Sciences and Technologies
institutions.englishBachelors: Three bachelor's in English (Biosystems Machinery and Technologies, Information Technologies for Sustainable Development, Sociology of Organisations and Public Administration), plus six-year Veterinary Medicine in English at EUR 9,600 a year
institutions.note: Outside Riga, in Jelgava, and the place to look for veterinary medicine in English. Non-visa applicants apply by 15 July for a September start; the application fee for EU citizens is EUR 160.

institutions.name: Ventspils University of Applied Sciences
institutions.englishBachelors: Two: Computer Science and Start-Up Management, autumn intake only
institutions.note: A small coastal university with a radio astronomy centre, and two English-taught bachelor's: Computer Science, and Start-Up Management. EU applicants have until 30 July and pay a EUR 100 application fee (dates as published for the autumn 2026 intake).

institutions.name: Art Academy of Latvia
institutions.note: Latvia's national art academy, with portfolio-based entry. Its English pages (September 2026) describe exchange study and a joint master's in Service Design and Innovations, and no English-taught bachelor's degree for a degree-seeking student.
institutions.admissionsUrlNote: Checked 2026-09-23. The Art Academy publishes no standing admissions page. The URL previously recorded here — lma.lv/en/admission — is a soft 404, and the cycle page the site itself used, /en/studies/admission-2023-2, has been taken down rather than renewed. Each year's rules are issued instead as Latvian-language PDFs under lma.lv/data/, and applications are taken through the portal at apply.lma.lv. Worth knowing before applying: the entrance examinations are conducted in Latvian.

institutions.name: Jazeps Vitols Latvian Academy of Music
institutions.englishBachelors: Bachelor teaching is mainly in Latvian; English-taught bachelor options not confirmed here
institutions.note: The national conservatoire; entry is by audition and you should expect Latvian in the bachelor programmes.

institutions.name: Transport and Telecommunication Institute
institutions.englishBachelors: Seven bachelor's on its English programme page: Computer Science (one track a double degree in AI), Computer Engineering and Electronics, Robotics, Transport and Logistics, Aviation Engineering, and Business and Management
institutions.note: Private, applied and unusually English-heavy for Latvia, with aviation and logistics programmes you will not find at the state universities.
